teacherTips: A seventh chord is a triad plus one more note. CM7 = C·E·G·B!
After G7 you'll want to land on C — that's called resolution.
To turn major into minor, lower the middle note (the 3rd) by a half step.
sus4 swaps the 3rd for the 4th: tension that loves to resolve back.
Change which note is at the bottom (an inversion) and the same chord feels new.
Dm7 – G7 – CM7 is the ii–V–I, the most common move in jazz.
Small hands? Drop the 5th. The 3rd and 7th give a chord its character.
Slow and accurate always beats fast and wrong.

cards.am7: A little wistful but soft. Good for rainy days.
cards.dm7: Where jazz begins: the 'ii' in ii–V–I.
cards.g7: Restless and itching to move. Resolve it to C.
cards.fmaj7: Like sunlight — it opens a song right up.
cards.em7: Light, clear minor that glides between chords.
cards.bm7b5: Half-diminished and mysterious; the ii of a minor key.
cards.csus4: Suspense waiting to resolve. Let it fall to C.
